title: Human Expert Evaluation of Agentic AI for EO, form F15
description:
Thank you for helping us evaluate the performance of different LLMs in Agentic AI frameworks for EO!

WHAT THIS IS
We built a benchmark to test the performance of different LLMs in agentic settings. This evaluation form is to compare the answers given by these LLMs when answering a question using different tools related to the agentic framework that we built - including different EO endpoints (Copernicus/Sentinel, Landsat), ERA5 climate data, EO Dashboard narratives, ESA science strategy documents, GIS analysis and scientific literature search.

You will be given 8 questions, and for each question you see every anonymous answer that assistant actually produced for it -- usually several, occasionally just one if only one assistant answered that particular question.

WHAT YOU DO
(About 34 minutes for this form -- your progress is saved in this browser, so it's fine to do this over more than one sitting.) The form will guide you through it, but for every question you will
1. Rate how relevant and realistic the question is for EO users.
2. Score the accuracy of each answer shown.
3. If there's more than one answer, rank them all from best to worst (skip this step when only one answer is shown -- there's nothing to compare it to).

HOW TO JUDGE ACCURACY
Judge scientific and domain correctness, and whether the answer addresses every part of the question. A minority of answers (marked "▣ image" next to the answer letter) include the actual image the assistant looked at -- check the description against it directly. For every other answer you cannot open the files or images it says it produced: treat claims that you find implausible or unsupported as errors. Do not reward length or formatting. If you cannot judge a question, say so in the comment field and give your best estimate.

Answers were produced automatically and may contain errors. Local file paths were removed from the answers. Long answers are collapsed by default — click an answer to expand it.

PRIVACY
Your name is recorded so we can follow up if needed, and is not shown to other experts. Responses are used only for the research evaluation of this benchmark and are reported in aggregate. Participation is voluntary; you can stop at any time by closing the page.

profile_fields.title: Name
profile_fields.help: So we know who a response came from. Not shown to other experts.

profile_fields.title: How would you rate your Earth Observation expertise?
Which areas are you experienced in?
choices: Climate and atmospheric data (ERA5, trace gases)
EO science strategy and scientific literature

profile_fields.title: Consent
choices: I agree that my responses are used for the research evaluation of this benchmark.

relevance.title: How relevant and realistic is this question for EO users (researchers, analysts, practitioners)?
relevance.help: 1 = not relevant or unrealistic; 3 = plausible but marginal or somewhat artificial; 5 = highly relevant and realistic.

accuracy.title: Accuracy: how correct and complete is each answer?
accuracy.help: 1 = incorrect or unusable; 2 = mostly incorrect or major omissions; 3 = partially correct or incomplete; 4 = mostly correct, minor issues; 5 = correct and complete. Equal scores are allowed.

ranking.title: Ranking: order all answers from best to worst.
ranking.help: Drag, or use the arrows, to put the best answer at the top and the worst at the bottom. Ties are not allowed.

familiarity.title: How familiar are you with the topic of this question?

comment.title: Comment (optional)
comment.help: For example: an error you spotted, why a question is not relevant, or that you could not judge it.

items.label: Cross-agent Synthesis
items.question: Find the EO Dashboard narrative about extreme air pollution episodes in Northern India and Pakistan, identify a representative city discussed in the narrative, and retrieve Sentinel-5P atmospheric composition data for that location during the smog season. Describe the spatial distribution of pollutant concentrations and explain how the observations relate to the pollution episode described in the narrative.

answers.text:
Based on the EO Dashboard narrative and the Sentinel-5P atmospheric data for Delhi, India, here is the analysis of the extreme air pollution episode:

Representative City:
The narrative "Extreme air pollution episodes in Northern India and Pakistan" identifies the Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP) as the primary region of concern, encompassing Northern India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh. While it does not focus on a single specific city, Delhi, India, is a representative urban center within this region and is well-documented for its severe winter smog episodes.

Spatial Distribution of Pollutant Concentrations:
The Sentinel-5P NO2 data for Delhi during the smog season (November-December 2023) reveals a distinct spatial pattern:
• The image shows NO2 column concentrations in greyscale, with brighter areas indicating higher concentrations.
• The urban core of Delhi exhibits significantly elevated NO2 levels, appearing as bright spots in the image.
• This pattern is consistent with the narrative's description of intense industrial and agricultural activities in the IGP, which contribute to high pollution levels.
• The spatial distribution highlights the concentration of pollution in urban areas, with lower concentrations observed in surrounding rural regions.

Relation to the Pollution Episode:
The observations directly correlate with the pollution episode described in the narrative:
• The high NO2 concentrations in Delhi's urban core align with the narrative's focus on the IGP as a region of intense pollution.
• The winter smog season in Delhi is characterized by temperature inversions that trap pollutants near the surface, leading to the observed high concentrations.
• The data visually confirms the narrative's assertion that the region experiences severe air pollution episodes, posing significant health risks to the local population.
• The spatial distribution of pollutants underscores the impact of urbanization and industrial activities on air quality in the IGP region.

In summary, the Sentinel-5P data for Delhi provides concrete evidence of the extreme air pollution episode described in the EO Dashboard narrative, demonstrating the spatial concentration of pollutants in urban areas and validating the narrative's findings about the health risks associated with poor air quality in the Indo-Gangetic Plain.

items.question: Download hourly ERA5 2 m air temperature over Alentejo region in Portugal for January 2023, aggregate the sub-daily values into daily mean temperatures, and identify the warmest and coldest days of the month.

answers.text:
The hourly ERA5 2 m air temperature data for January 2023 over the Alentejo region in Portugal has been successfully downloaded. The file is available at:

File: era5_2m_temp_hourly_alentejo_2023_01.nc

However, the aggregation of hourly data into daily means and the identification of the warmest and coldest days could not be completed automatically due to tool limitations.

To proceed with the analysis, you can use the following Python code in a local environment with xarray and pandas installed:

import xarray as xr
import pandas as pd

Load the data
ds = xr.open_dataset('era5_2m_temp_hourly_alentejo_2023_01.nc')

Convert valid_time to datetime
ds = ds.rename({'valid_time': 'time'})
ds['time'] = pd.to_datetime(ds['time'].values)

Resample to daily means
daily_mean = ds['t2m'].resample(time='D').mean()

Identify warmest and coldest days
warmest_day = daily_mean.idxmax(dim='time')
coldest_day = daily_mean.idxmin(dim='time')

print(f"Warmest day: {warmest_day.values}, Temperature: {daily_mean.sel(time=warmest_day).values} K")
print(f"Coldest day: {coldest_day.values}, Temperature: {daily_mean.sel(time=coldest_day).values} K")

This will:
1. Aggregate the hourly data into daily means.
2. Identify the warmest and coldest days of January 2023.
3. Print the results.

However, the data has been successfully downloaded to:
alentejo_t2m_2023_01.nc

items.question: Find the EO Dashboard narrative about COVID-19 travel restrictions disrupting global cargo shipping, identify a representative shipping chokepoint, and retrieve Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 imagery for that location. Use the SAR data to assess maritime activity and the optical image to describe the surrounding port infrastructure and geographic context.

answers.text:
Based on the Sentinel-2 true-color imagery of the Suez Canal, Egypt, captured during the COVID-19 restrictions (2020-2021), here is an analysis of the surrounding port infrastructure and geographic context:

Geographic Context:
• The Suez Canal is a narrow waterway cutting through the desert, connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.
• The surrounding landscape is predominantly arid and desert-like, with sparse vegetation.
• The canal is flanked by urban development and port infrastructure, particularly along its northern and southern termini.

Port Infrastructure:
• Northern Terminal (Port of Suez): The northern end of the canal features a well-developed port area with visible industrial facilities, warehouses, and shipping terminals.
• Southern Terminal (Port of Port Said): The southern end shows a more compact port infrastructure, with docks and berths for cargo ships.
• Canal Banks: The banks of the canal are lined with infrastructure, including roads, pipelines, and possibly rail lines, facilitating the movement of goods and personnel.

Maritime Activity:
• While the Sentinel-2 imagery does not provide SAR data to assess maritime activity, the visible presence of ships and port facilities indicates that the Suez Canal remained operational during the COVID-19 restrictions.
• The canal's strategic importance as a global shipping chokepoint is evident from the dense infrastructure and the continued presence of vessels, despite the global disruptions caused by the pandemic.

Conclusion:
The Suez Canal, as depicted in the Sentinel-2 imagery, remains a critical maritime artery, with its port infrastructure and surrounding areas showcasing the resilience of global trade even during periods of significant disruption. The canal's continued operation highlights its vital role in international commerce, despite the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic.

Note: Sentinel-1 SAR data, which would have been used to assess maritime activity, could not be retrieved due to a persistent server-side error. However, the optical imagery provides valuable context regarding the port infrastructure and geographic setting of this critical shipping chokepoint.
